ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Renal consequences of deposition

A 58-year-old woman with biopsy-proven renal amyloidosis develops dependent edema. Her urine contains 7 g of protein daily and serum albumin is 2.1 g/dL. Which mechanism best explains the fall in plasma oncotic pressure?

  1. Urinary loss of albumin through a damaged glomerular barrier
  2. Increased renal synthesis of albumin
  3. Selective failure of collecting-duct water transport
  4. Increased erythrocyte destruction
  5. Complete cessation of glomerular filtration
Answer and explanation

Urinary loss of albumin through a damaged glomerular barrier

Glomerular deposition disrupts filtration barrier selectivity, allowing albumin loss and producing nephrotic syndrome.

Option explanations

Urinary loss of albumin through a damaged glomerular barrier: Glomerular deposition disrupts filtration barrier selectivity, allowing albumin loss and producing nephrotic syndrome.

Increased renal synthesis of albumin: Albumin is synthesized predominantly in the liver; increased synthesis would not explain depletion.

Selective failure of collecting-duct water transport: This primarily affects urine concentration rather than causing heavy albuminuria.

Increased erythrocyte destruction: Hemolysis does not explain the measured urinary protein loss.

Complete cessation of glomerular filtration: Her heavy protein excretion implies ongoing filtration; anuria is not the mechanism shown.
